upstream.repository_description: German-language voice AI agent — Fritzbox SIP + PJSIP + Qwen3-ASR/TTS + Nous Hermes on DGX Spark

scope: Source-only audit. No upstream code execution, dependency installation, model download, target-host execution, F2 integration, German E2E benchmark, room-microphone AEC test or Trigger-4 acceptance was performed.

evidence.finding: The pinned source describes a German local voice path using PJSUA2 16 kHz PCM -> VAD -> Qwen3-ASR -> local LLM/tool loop -> Qwen3-TTS -> PCM/RTP, with LLM-token segmentation and sentence-level synthesis/playback overlap.

Barge-in is causally fenced by a per-call generation counter. Speech during SPEAKING/PROCESSING increments generation, marks previous_response_interrupted, cancels and awaits the old playback task, clears the sink, resets VAD, then starts the replacement streamed turn.

The streaming path appends the assistant response to history only after the full producer/consumer path completes. A cancellation before completion therefore does not append the partial assistant response. The next LLM call receives a one-shot German system context saying the previous response was interrupted and must not be continued unprompted.

Production TTS streaming is sentence-granular, not codec/sample-native: each completed sentence uses the stable whole-WAV TTS endpoint, then yields bounded PCM blocks. At most two completed sentence segments may prefetch.

Smart Turn v3 is revision-pinned and in-process ONNX, but the constructor calls hf_hub_download when no injected test session is provided. Unmodified adoption therefore does not satisfy Frankenstein's zero-network target-runtime invariant unless the artifact is pre-provisioned and loading is changed/fenced to local-only.

Source tests exercise stream cancellation under a full output queue, bounded playback backlog, playback-error clearing, and a real PJSIP barge-in path that waits for the old producer finalizer before starting clean replacement output. These are source/test assets only; this Trigger-7 audit did not execute them.

The upstream README reports short German acceptance probes of 282 ms ASR, 861 ms non-streaming TTS and 609 ms to a diagnostic stream chunk on NVIDIA GB10. These values are not percentile characterization and grant zero Frankenstein runtime credit.

No recognized project license was observed at the pinned revision. The repository API reports license=null and pyproject.toml declares no license. This audit therefore treats the project as an architecture/test donor only, not a directly reusable code donor.

transferable_mechanisms: generation-fenced cancellation of stale voice output
sink/playback-buffer clear on interruption or streaming failure
one-shot interrupted-response context on the next model turn
byte-bounded playback backlog rather than unbounded item queues
revision-pinned in-process turn detector with explicit CPU thread caps
nontransferable_or_unproven: The telephony/SIP acoustic path is not evidence for Frankenstein room-microphone/open-speaker AEC robustness.
Sentence-level whole-WAV TTS is not evidence for true sample-native low-latency synthesis.
README latency probes are hardware- and stack-specific upstream measurements, not F2 measurements.
hf_hub_download at runtime conflicts with F2 zero-network target-runtime requirements unless replaced by pre-provisioned local artifact loading.
Direct source-code reuse is not admitted while license status remains unresolved.
hypothesis: The highest-value donor contribution is not the upstream model stack but its causal turn-state discipline: generation fencing + cancellation finalization + playback clearing + conservative assistant-history commit can prevent Frankenstein from reasoning from speech the human never heard.
counterhypothesis: The apparent robustness is dominated by telephony transport semantics; without an explicit room-audio AEC/reference path the same VAD/barge-in controller may self-trigger on Frankenstein's own speaker output and fail in the target interaction geometry.
cheapest_high_information_discriminator: Port only the protocol semantics, not the code: add/verify deterministic F2 voice-harness tests for stale-generation rejection, cancellation-finalizer ordering, unheard-assistant non-commit, playback-buffer clearing and bounded ahead-audio. Separately require a pre-provisioned local turn-model artifact and open-speaker AEC loopback before any target-runtime promotion.
